terms.def: Applying for a green card from inside the United States, rather than at a consulate abroad.

Permission for someone without a visa to travel abroad and be readmitted. For TPS holders the document is Form I-512T, and being admitted on it can matter a great deal for a later green-card application.
The country a person counts against for immigrant-visa numbers, usually their country of birth. Haiti is not listed separately in the Visa Bulletin, so it falls under "All Chargeability Areas."
The Secretary of Homeland Security's decision that conditions in a country warrant TPS. Designations are made for 6 to 18 months and must be reviewed before they expire.
Employment Authorization Document, Form I-766. A work card, not a status.
An extension continues TPS for people who already have it. A redesignation also opens it to people who arrived more recently, up to a new cutoff date.
The date in the Visa Bulletin at which a green card may actually be approved for a given category and country.
The entry requirement in INA 245(a). Someone who crossed without being inspected has not met it, which is why the travel-authorization question matters.
The date a petition was filed. It fixes a person's place in line.
The immigration court process, run by EOIR within the Department of Justice, that determines whether a person may be removed from the United States.
The Secretary's decision to end a country's TPS designation. By statute it takes effect no sooner than 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.
A decision undoing a prior action. In February 2025 DHS partially vacated the 2024 Haiti extension; a federal court later held the Secretary lacked authority to do that.
The gap between publication of a termination notice and its effective date. It is a statutory minimum on the notice, not a grant of extra benefits.
